scenes.headline:
The next AI bottleneck
isn't intelligence.
scenes.body: It's control after the model starts taking action.

scenes.headline: Visibility comes first.
scenes.body: You need to know what the agent is doing, where, and why.

scenes.headline: Access should be explicit.
scenes.body: Reading, drafting, executing, publishing and spending are different permissions.

scenes.headline:
Production agents
need evaluation loops.
scenes.body: Reliability has to improve as workflows, policies and user behavior change.

scenes.headline:
Autonomy needs
a stop condition.
scenes.body: Retries, escalation and rollback should be designed before failure happens.

scenes.headline:
Scale autonomy
with boundaries.
scenes.body: The useful question is not only what an agent can do—but what it is allowed to finish.

publish.title: The Next AI Bottleneck Isn't Intelligence. It's Control. #Shorts
publish.caption:
AI agents are moving into production. The operational bottleneck is increasingly control: visibility, explicit permissions, evaluation loops, stop conditions and rollback. OpenAI and IBM are both emphasizing the systems needed to run agents reliably—not just stronger models.

Practical implementation kit: https://stratumpraxis.com/agentic-ai-governance-permission-kit.html?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=agent-control-20260827
